evidence: Exemption: explicit code labels in the paper - the S1 Appendix legend names each of the 105 codes (e.g. 'r_ods089 = eat soup', 'r_ods018 = run'), and codes are the .xls's own column names melted unchanged, so every item is distinguished from every other by its own label. Corroboration that the labels sit on the right columns (verify_hermans_2015_dm1_rods.R): route 1-style, paper Table 2 Rasch locations for the 25 final items, mapped to codes via the legend, vs live difficulty 1-mean/2: Spearman rho=0.994 (random-permutation null max 0.721 over 5000), e.g. eat soup -3.305/0.079, get out of bed -1.777/0.213, walk 3 flights 2.832/0.603, run (>=30 y) 3.904/0.712. Route 8, nested tasks all monotone: stairs 1<2<3 0.375<0.480<0.603; outdoor <100m<<1km<>1km 0.296<0.494<0.603; stand <15 min<for hours 0.392<0.748; wash face<entire body 0.071<0.173; even<uneven ground 0.235<0.514. The statistical routes alone pin ~35 of 105 items; they would not catch a legend swap between two unanchored items of similar difficulty (e.g. read a book / read a newspaper) - those rest on the legend label. Table 2 'carry and put down heavy object (10 kg)' taken as r_ods053 (0.673) not r_ods052 lift (0.659). Option axis: S1 Fig anchors (0)/(1)/(2); legend's '3 = without difficulty' is a typo (raw holds only 0/1/2).
